entries.mechanism: EUROMOD BE_2025 tinfe_be subtracts the 880 EUR refundable activity credit before tinmu_be computes the 7.17% Flanders communal addition. The statutory order computes the addition before imputing the credit, so EUROMOD understates tax by exactly 880 x 7.17% = 63.096 EUR (ec-jrc issue #24).

Three quantified EUROMOD-side mechanisms close the mixed worker and self-employment residual. RuleSpec applies 20.5% secondary-activity SSC to the full 20,000 EUR (4,100 EUR), while EUROMOD applies it only above 1,881.76 EUR (3,714.2392 EUR), a 385.7608 EUR net-income difference. RuleSpec worker SSC is 1,591.35 EUR versus EUROMOD's 3,921 - 3,398.52 = 522.48 EUR, and its forfait is 5,930 EUR versus 5,929.995 EUR, another 1,068.875 EUR of worker-net difference. The resulting -1,454.6358 EUR RuleSpec taxable-base difference adds 701.520288424719 EUR of tax in the fixed-credit counterfactual. EUROMOD's uncapped work-bonus credit then removes 552.615720 EUR relative to the credit on the reduction actually granted (existing issue #12 disposition), and subtracting the 1,504.848888 EUR credit before the 7.17% Flanders addition removes another 107.8976652696 EUR (ec-jrc issue #24). Their 41.006903155119 EUR sum closes the observed EUROMOD-minus-Axiom residual to displayed-float precision.

EUROMOD BE_2025 neg_be/Max overwrites the requested -1,000 EUR yse value with zero, leaving 7,000 EUR of taxable worker income. The merged RuleSpec fixture applies Article 23 current-period activity netting and subtracts the 1,000 EUR self-employment loss, yielding 6,000 EUR. The named clipping mechanism therefore explains the full +1,000 EUR EUROMOD-minus-Axiom taxable-income residual.
